summary:
Nuevo León sits under Mexico's national framework; the findings below are specific to the state. Its penal code does not typify transfeminicidio. A bill to add the offence was filed, ignored for a year and allowed to lapse, so a fresh filing was required. A trans visitor assaulted in Nuevo León has no state-level aggravated homicide category for anti-trans violence.

Three trans women were killed in Nuevo León in under a week in July 2024. One was Arantza Castillo, 23, killed while doing sex work; another was found dead in a motel on 27 June 2024 and had not been identified. The state justice ministry issued no case information on any of them.

Civil-society tallies for 2024 record four transfeminicides in Nuevo León. Asamblea Nacional Trans No Binarie counted at least four in the state that year; Verificado recorded four transfeminicides alongside seven attacks on LGBT people and three forced disappearances. These are raw counts, not rates, and the sources supply no per-capita denominator or comparison with the state's general homicide rate, so they do not by themselves establish how much of the risk is trans-specific.
tangentialFactors:
Letra S's annual hate-crime yearbook recorded five LGBT+ homicides in Nuevo León in 2024, behind only Mexico City's 17, of which 11 were trans women. The comparison is a raw-count ranking: Nuevo León has a smaller population than Mexico City and the source gives no per-capita rate, so the ordering does not establish that a visitor faces more risk per resident in Nuevo León.

The state's 2024 figures come from civil-society monitoring. No official state count of anti-trans violence was identified.
localsOnly:
A state labour diagnostic found 42.2% of Nuevo León's trans population unemployed and 35.1% reporting discrimination at work.

Colectivo Casa Trans has led the campaign to typify transfeminicidio in the state penal code, including a plantón of more than 50 days outside the state congress as of 12 January 2026; its first bill lapsed after a year without action and a new filing was required.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether other Nuevo León provisions cover anti-trans violence is not established by the sources; they document only the absence of a transfeminicidio offence.

The identity of the woman found dead in a motel on 27 June 2024 remains unresolved, and the state justice ministry's refusal to release case information leaves the investigation status of all three July 2024 killings unknown.

No per-capita rate of anti-trans violence for Nuevo León, and no comparison with the state's general homicide rate, is available; the counts above are raw figures from civil-society monitoring that the sources describe as undercounting where victims are unnamed or gender data is missing.
